tools.cron.status: Scheduler-wide counts of enabled jobs, queued runs, and running runs. Scope to one schedule by `id` for that job's scheduler state: enabled, schedule, last run time and status, queued/running runs, and next run time.
tools.cron.list: List schedule summaries with lifecycle owners.
tools.cron.view: View one schedule's details by id.
tools.cron.add: Add a new scheduled cron job. Definition file paths are chosen automatically from the job id and schedule; never provide them. Before adding, list existing jobs and reuse or update one instead of creating overlapping schedules.
tools.cron.update: Update an existing schedule. If you leave out `at`, the runtime chooses a start when switching to an interval, or resets a start it chose when you change how often the interval runs. Other fields you leave out stay the same.
tools.cron.run: Enqueue an immediate manual run of a schedule by `id`.
tools.cron.runs: Recent run records (status, timing, attempt, error text), optionally scoped to one schedule by `id`.
tools.cron.stop: Stop a schedule's in-flight run by `id`. Cancels the run that is currently executing — its worker and subagents included — records it as cancelled by <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end -->, and tells the main agent that the run was stopped. When nothing is running, pending queued occurrences are cancelled silently instead. Pass `run` to stop one exact run from `cron.runs`. The schedule itself is unchanged and still fires at its next occurrence; use `cron.update` with `enabled: false` to pause it or `cron.remove` to delete it. Use this when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asks to stop, cancel, or abort a scheduled job that is running right now.

fields.retry: Optional for `cron.add` and `cron.update`: automatic retry policy for runtime failures and timeouts. Worker-reported incomplete results and already-dispatched artifact actions are excluded.
fields.retry.on_failure: Whether to retry runs that fail from runtime errors or timeouts. Default false. Worker-reported incomplete results and already-dispatched artifact actions are never retried automatically because their effects may have committed.
fields.id: Stable job id. Required by `cron.add`, `cron.update`, `cron.view`, `cron.remove`, `cron.run`, and `cron.stop`; optional on `cron.status` and `cron.runs` to scope the result. Follow the job-id naming rules in the namespace description.
fields.title:
Optional for `action=add|update`: single-line display label, at most 120
characters. On update, omission preserves the label and an empty string clears
it. The stable job id remains the identity.
fields.enabled: Required for `cron.add`; optional for `cron.update`. `false` keeps the definition but scheduler will not queue runs.
fields.mode: Required for `cron.add`; optional for `cron.update`. Must be `task` when provided.
fields.body: Optional for `cron.add` and `cron.update`: markdown body written after frontmatter. This carries the complete execute-phase task intent. Describe the work and the desired result or delivery intent semantically, including when no chat report is wanted even though background data changes. Do not name the terminal tools `nothing_to_do`, `nothing_to_report`, or `notify_main_agent`; validation rejects those names because later resolution and relay phases implement that intent. This restriction changes only delivery mechanics, not the task or requested outcome. Do not instruct the worker to edit `MEMORY.md`; observations go to the daily log `~/memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`.
fields.prompt: Optional for `cron.add` and `cron.update`: body text fallback when `body` is omitted.
fields.timeout_secs: Optional for `cron.add` and `cron.update`: expected execution budget, from 1 to 86400 seconds. For recurring jobs, the runtime enforces `min(86400, max(requested timeout, time between scheduled runs))`; an omitted request defaults to 3600s. Set a larger value when the task may need longer than its cadence. The cadence allowance is a full schedule interval, not the time remaining until the next firing. One-off jobs default to 86400s and honor an explicit value. The response reports `requested_timeout_secs`, the effective `timeout_secs`, and a `timeout_note` explaining any extension. Use the effective value when explaining the schedule. Calendar gaps may vary by occurrence; an already-started occurrence keeps its assigned budget. Existing concurrency rules still apply.
fields.include_disabled: For `cron.list`: include disabled schedules when true.
fields.run: For `cron.stop`: the exact run to stop, a `run_id` from `cron.runs`. Omit it to stop the schedule's currently running run, or its queued occurrences when nothing is running.
fields.schedule: Required for `cron.add`; optional for `cron.update`. Required nested fields by `kind`: `runonce` needs `at`; `interval` needs `every` (`at` optional; omitted means the runtime picks the start, first run within about one cadence); `daily` needs `time`; `weekly` needs `time` and `dow`; `monthly` needs `time` and `dom`; `yearly` needs `time`, `dom`, and `month`. On add, every kind but `interval` also needs `timing`; `anytime` takes no `time`. `timezone` applies to every kind; on add it may be omitted and defaults to the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's current<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's default<!-- group-only:end --> timezone, and the add result reports what was used.
fields.schedule.kind: Schedule kind; see the schedule field requirements.
fields.schedule.timezone: Optional on add: when omitted, the job uses the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's current timezone<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's default timezone, the `timezone` in GROUP.md's frontmatter<!-- group-only:end --> (recurring kinds store `@user.current` and follow <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->that default<!-- group-only:end -->; runonce and interval store the zone resolved at creation), and the result reports the timezone used, so repeat it back when confirming the schedule. <!-- personal-only:start -->If no current timezone is known yet, the call is rejected and an explicit timezone is required<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Set it to the asking member's timezone from their GROUP.md entry when the time is that member's local time, and ask that member in the group first when their entry has none<!-- group-only:end -->. Explicit values: an IANA timezone (`UTC`, `America/New_York`), or <!-- personal-only:start -->a symbolic ref:<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the symbolic ref<!-- group-only:end --> `@user.current` <!-- personal-only:start -->(the user's current timezone). Symbolic refs are valid only for recurring kinds; runonce and interval need a literal IANA timezone<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->for the group's default, which is valid only for recurring kinds; runonce and interval need a literal IANA timezone<!-- group-only:end -->. Set it explicitly when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> names a specific timezone or place.
fields.schedule.at:
Local wall-clock datetime `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` interpreted in `schedule.timezone`; no `Z` or numeric offset. For `kind=interval`, leave out `at` when creating or editing a schedule if the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->request<!-- group-only:end --> only said how often to run. Do not add `at` just to move the next run to a round hour. If <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> gives a start time, set `at` to that time. If <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asks for runs at specific clock times but gives no start time, set `at` to the next one. Quarter-hour-aligned runs are deliberately dispatched up to five minutes early to spread load: set the exact `at` asked for, but describe the timing back as approximate.
For `kind=runonce`, a past `at` is accepted and fires an immediate catch-up run. Never book a past `at` for a future intent: when the stated time has already passed, surface the discrepancy and confirm, proposing the next future reading when one is plain.
fields.schedule.timing: `exact`: <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> named this time, it is tied to an event, or it is set relative to now; kept as given. `window`: you chose the time, or only a part of the day is settled; the window starts at `time` (or `at`), and the runtime saves one time inside it, fixed for this machine. `anytime`: no time of day matters; the runtime saves this machine's daily time, and a `runonce` `at` sets only the date. A `window` or `anytime` `runonce` that lands in the past moves to the next day.
fields.schedule.window: Length of the `timing=window` window: `15m` to `12h`; default `1h`, or the saved length on update.
fields.schedule.dow: `Mon..Sun`. Honored only for `kind=weekly`; other kinds silently ignore it. No kind expresses nth-weekday-of-month ("first Monday"): `monthly` fires on fixed `dom` days only. Say so and offer an exact alternative (a weekly job whose task skips non-matching weeks); never store a plain weekly or monthly job as if it matched.
fields.notification_requested: Set true when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asked for this reminder, recurring update or watch. Set false when arranging it on your own initiative. Interest in a topic alone is not a request for notifications. On unrelated updates, leave this field out to preserve the existing intent. Use `schedule.timing` separately to say whether the time can move.
fields.owner: Optional namespaced lifecycle owner; an owned schedule is deleted alongside its owner. Every reminder or follow-up names the goal or tracked item it serves as `goal:<goal-slug>`; a reminder serving no existing goal gets its own tracked item first and uses that item's slug. A bare reminder cron with no owner is a routing error. Omit the owner only on a schedule that serves no goal or tracked item. Supported: `goal:<goal-slug>` (goal-owned, stored goal slug). Goal-owned cron output stays in that goal's workspace: documents <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asked for in `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/files/`, everything else in `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/hidden_files/`.

texts.small_hours: It is currently the small hours of the user's night, and this one-shot fires more than 20 hours from now. If the user asked for tonight, this morning, or tomorrow, the stored day is probably one day late: shortly after midnight, 'tomorrow morning' means the morning only a few hours away. Check the wait above against the request before confirming; if the user truly meant the later day, this schedule is fine.
texts.runs_note: These runs show whether the job ran, not whether the user saw anything. Check the chat before telling the user a result was delivered.
texts.scheduled_run_self_change: A scheduled run can't change its own instructions. Describe the change you want and why in your final response; the chat agent that owns this job will confirm it with the user before applying anything.
